evidence.detail: The class recognizes @type@, <type>, </type> and <type=N> markup, strips those tags for plain-text output, and rewrites opening type tags into timestamped <type=speed:timestamp> state.
Default type speed is 75 ms per visible character; explicit <type=N> speed is clamped to 10..2000 ms. The parser computes the visible character count from (now-timestamp)/speed + 1.

Client constructs exactly one rs/l/A instance, runs rendered text through it after the flashing processor, and queries its active-state predicate to decide whether time-driven text requires another redraw.

Both exact-v308 font/text renderers rs/l/h and rs/l/k invoke the class's static type-tag parsing helpers while measuring/rendering strings, proving this is part of the live text-effect pipeline rather than an isolated formatter.

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the <type> time-based progressive reveal processor; original stripped identifier is not claimed.

evidence.detail: The class recognizes @fla@, @fla2@, <fla>, <fla2>, </fla>, </fla2>, <fla=N> and <fla2=N>, rewriting active openings into timestamp-bearing fla/fla2 tags.
The static render-state function alternates the supplied text color with a hidden/sentinel state every 200 ms; fla uses a 600 ms active window while fla2 uses 1200 ms.

Client constructs exactly one rs/l/l instance, runs text through it before rs/l/A, and polls its active-state predicate so flashing text continues to invalidate/redraw while its timing window is live.
The live rs/l/h and rs/l/k font renderers call the fla/fla2 tag recognizers, timestamp parser and color-state function directly during string rendering.

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the fla/fla2 timed visibility/color effect processor; original stripped identifier is not claimed.
